_THIS_IS_NOT_A_PRODUCTION_FILE: EXAMPLES ONLY. Every scenario below is an ILLUSTRATION written to make a question answerable, not an answer to it. None is a recommendation. Copying any of them to THRESHOLDS.json would set a production trust gate, which is a Founder-only act (G1).
_do_not_create: THRESHOLDS.json. Round 5 Lane A3 is forbidden from creating it, from recommending a point on the curve, and from claiming any gate is met. While THRESHOLDS.json is absent the pipeline reports trusted = 0 and prints why — that is the system working, not a bug.
_written_by: Round 5 · Lane A3 (role spec + trust-gate sensitivity), Founder order §8
_read_before_using: docs/research/TRUST-GATE-SENSITIVITY.md — the method, the curve, and the questions a gate needs answered first
docs/research/ROLE-DEFINITION-SPEC-v1.md — several gates below key on a ROLE, and role is the class the two blind annotators disagree on (κ 0.423–0.713)

docs/research/METRIC-DENOMINATORS.md — D5. These scenarios are evaluated on the gold plane (54 pages / 643 learning blocks). They are NOT evaluated on 3,679 or 3,381 lessons and must never be quoted as if they were.
_how_a_gate_is_evaluated: tool/corpus/thresholds/run.py replays each gate over frozen per-block evidence rows and reports coverage · correct served · wrong served · teaching-critical served · withheld · false withheld · restored · restore precision. It ranks nothing.

_guard_classes.fidelity: agree_text · agree_tones · agree_numbers · agree_order · math_guard · unit_guard · chem_guard · low_ocr_conf · line_structure — 'is the served string what the page prints?'. Waiving one is a genuine coverage/accuracy trade and shows up on the curve.
_guard_classes.policy: teacher_text · answer_leak · figure_text · figure_dependent · page_feature:* · box_boundary · role_conflict — 'may a child be shown this at all?'. The gold plane can only say whether such a block is a faithful copy; it CANNOT say whether serving it is allowed. Waiving one is not a fidelity trade and the curve must not be read as if it were.
_guard_classes.structural: empty_block · furniture · empty — waiving them serves nothing.

scenarios.name: A · conservative-illustration
scenarios.illustrates: What if today's guards are kept AND a character-exact agreement floor plus a high role-confidence floor are added on top? The question it answers: how much coverage does 'tighter than today' still cost?

scenarios.name: B · tone-signal-illustration
scenarios.illustrates: What if Lane A1's Vietnamese third signal (lexicon) resolved tone disagreements, so `agree_tones` no longer had to withhold on its own? `agree_tones` is the single largest over-withholder measured on the gold plane. This scenario is a DEPENDENCY, not a decision: it is only reachable if that signal exists and its false-correction rate is measured.

scenarios.name: C · balanced-illustration
scenarios.illustrates: What if the two OCR stacks disagreeing about TONES or about WORDING no longer withheld by themselves, but a numeric agreement floor replaced them? The point of the scenario is to show that replacing a categorical guard with a numeric floor is not free — it changes which blocks are refused, not only how many.

scenarios.name: D · coverage-leaning-illustration
scenarios.illustrates: What if every DISPLAY-level agreement guard were waived and only the guards that protect numbers, formulas, units and reading order remained? This is the shape of a 'the child may see a tone slip, never a wrong number' policy. It is shown so its cost is visible, not because it is advisable.

scenarios.name: E · policy-only-illustration (far end of the curve)
scenarios.illustrates: The end point: no fidelity guard at all, only the guards that answer 'may a child see this?'. Included so the curve has a measured right-hand edge. It serves everything the pipeline can read, wrong or right.

scenarios.name: F · question-surface-illustration
scenarios.illustrates: A DIFFERENT gate from the reading gate: what a Short-Answer surface would consume. Only blocks the role layer calls a question, at high role confidence, never figure-dependent. TC-19 #3 asks for QUESTION precision >= 0.95 before any auto-labelled question is graded; the role-signal experiment measured 0.938 at n = 16 and the gold set measures trusted-QUESTION precision 0.903 (n = 72). This scenario exists to show that a product surface needs its own gate, and that role — the class with κ 0.423–0.713 — is the thing it keys on.

scenarios.name: G · teaching-critical-floor-illustration
scenarios.illustrates: What if the gate were expressed as a floor on the SIGNAL rather than on the guard set: keep only structural guards, but require character-exact two-stack agreement. It asks whether one numeric floor can replace a hand-built guard set — and the answer the numbers give is the point of the scenario.

_audit_plane_note: The gold plane has a withheld side with ground truth, so it can measure RESTORE. The audit plane (the annotated false-trust samples) is almost entirely SERVED rows, so it can only answer the opposite question: what would this gate REMOVE from content the product ships today, and how much of what it removes is actually right? `restored` is meaningless there and reads 0.

audit_plane_scenarios.name: H · two-column-math-withhold-illustration
audit_plane_scenarios.illustrates: Round-3 measured false trust 0.804 on two-column pages vs 0.528 on single-column, and 0.878 on Toán. What would the product lose if every served row on a two-column page carrying math were withheld?

audit_plane_scenarios.name: I · subject-withhold-illustration (Toán)
audit_plane_scenarios.illustrates: The bluntest possible gate: withhold a whole subject. Shown because it is the cheapest thing to implement and the most expensive thing to live with — it is here to be compared against, not adopted.

audit_plane_scenarios.name: J · multi-line-withhold-illustration
audit_plane_scenarios.illustrates: Reading-order errors were only judgeable on rows with two or more printed lines (round-3: 0.306 on 324 such rows). What if every multi-line served row were withheld?

audit_plane_scenarios.name: K · ocr-agreement-floor-illustration
audit_plane_scenarios.illustrates: The audit rows carry an OCR-line similarity pre-check. What would a floor on it remove — and how much of that is right? Note the honest limit: this signal was a HINT shown to the annotator, never a gate, and it is null on 76 of the 484 round-3 rows.

_lesson_level_record_is_separate: docs/research/legacy-reprocess/THRESHOLDS.example.json (Lane D) is a LESSON-level template with a single `max_false_trust_rate`. This file is BLOCK-level and orthogonal: a lesson gate consumes the output of a block gate. Neither is a decision; do not merge them without deciding which denominator each is measured on.
_what_is_still_missing_before_any_gate_c: A denominator decision: the gold plane is 643 learning blocks on 54 pages, deliberately hard-selected. The shipped-content plane (3,334 served blocks) has no withheld side, so it cannot measure restore.
A cost asymmetry from the Founder: how many correct blocks withheld equal one wrong block served? Every point on the curve is an implicit answer to that question.

Whether display-only errors and teaching-critical errors go through the SAME gate. Round 3 measured them separately for exactly this reason (display-only false trust 0.293 vs teaching-critical 0.333 on the shipped sample).
Whether a policy guard (teacher_text, answer_leak) is ever waivable at all. The simulator can waive it; doctrine may not permit it.
The role definitions (ROLE-DEFINITION-SPEC-v1.md). Scenario F keys on a role, and role is the least reproducible class measured so far.
